indicator_definition: This indicator measures the proportion of persons aged 25 to 34 who have successfully completed tertiary education (ISCED 2011 levels 5–8). It is expressed as a percentage of the total population in that age group. Data are based on the EU Labour Force Survey.
rationale: Increasing tertiary educational attainment is key to developing a skilled workforce capable of driving innovation and economic growth. Higher levels of education are associated with better employment prospects, higher earnings and greater civic participation. Progress means a sustained rise in the share of young people completing tertiary education.
methodology_characteristics: Data are collected through the EU Labour Force Survey (EU-LFS). Tertiary education corresponds to ISCED 2011 levels 5 to 8, covering short-cycle tertiary education, bachelor's or equivalent, master's or equivalent, and doctoral or equivalent programmes. The age group 25–34 is chosen because most people in this range have completed their initial education.
